title: Today, I Lead the Table
teaser: After a late-night encounter at a back-alley sushi bar, Emiko names Ryuji first assistant for an open-chest coronary artery bypass graft the next morning.
gallery_caption: Following a late-night encounter at a back-alley sushi counter, Emiko Mido personally names Ryuji Sakaguchi first assistant for an open-chest coronary artery bypass graft—and slides her private bypass notebook across the desk afterward.

choices.choice_em3_c1_a: "Considering a certain surgical chief only opened her regular roster to me the other day—when it comes to a real fight, I know who belongs across the table."
choices.choice_em3_c1_b: "Don't tell me you actually keep tabs on who stands in my first-assistant spot?"
choices.choice_em3_c1_c: "When you share a department, you have to see everyone's strengths clearly—and nobody knows how sharp your blade is at the table better than I do."
choices.choice_em3_c2_a: Without waiting for a word, gently part and pad the epicardial fat groove with micro-forceps and a warm saline pledget, opening a clear running-suture lane ahead of her needle.
choices.choice_em3_c2_b: While steadying the LAD arteriotomy plane, call out the natural lie of the LIMA pedicle in half a breath to align her entry angle on the heel.
choices.choice_em3_c2_c: Hold crisp micro-tension across both edges of the arteriotomy, eye her single-snip bevel on the graft, and murmur a dry callback to last night's knife work.
choices.choice_em3_c3_a: "Then we settle it on merit. When the day comes that my name goes on that shortlist, I won't hold back either."
choices.choice_em3_c3_b: "Don't worry—I never planned on anyone stepping aside for me. Until that's settled, though, make sure you still call me in for fights like today's."
choices.choice_em3_c3_c: "You just lent me your prized bypass notes, Chief Mido—aren't you worried I'll master them and turn around to challenge you with them?"

nodes.em3_s1_01: By the time Ryuji Sakaguchi finished signing off on the last set of postoperative ward orders and stepped out of Hoshimi Hospital, most of the streetlights along the corner were already glowing.
nodes.em3_s1_02: Around the turn of the back alley behind the hospital stood an old-fashioned sushi bar with only eight counter seats. A plain indigo noren hung outside, and warm amber light still spilled onto the pavement well past nine—ideal for a surgeon getting off late to put something warm in his stomach.
nodes.em3_s1_03: Ryuji lifted the noren and stepped inside. The gentle scent of vinegared rice and steaming sencha drifted from behind the wooden counter. At this hour there were no other diners—only a familiar silhouette seated toward the far end.
nodes.em3_s1_04: Long silver-violet hair falling cleanly past her shoulders, a tailored thin trench coat resting beside her dark crimson top, her spine held ramrod straight even on a backless high wooden stool.
nodes.em3_s1_05: Emiko Mido sat there alone with a coarse ceramic teacup of hot tea before her, her gaze resting quietly on the hinoki cutting board behind the counter. She did not look lonely, much less as though she were waiting for someone—simply long accustomed to finishing a quiet dinner by herself.
nodes.em3_s1_06: Hearing the door slide open, the sushi chef looked up with a welcoming call:
nodes.em3_s1_07: "Welcome! Just one tonight? Please, take any seat you like."
nodes.em3_s1_08: At the sound, Emiko turned her head slightly, recognized Ryuji Sakaguchi without much surprise in her eyes, and gave the faintest nod.
nodes.em3_s1_09: Ryuji walked over and gestured toward the empty stool half an arm's length beside her:
nodes.em3_s1_11: Emiko glanced once at the wooden stool, drew her gaze back, and lifted her teacup for a sip.
nodes.em3_s1_13: Ryuji slipped off his coat, hung it up, took the seat beside her, and ordered a pot of hot tea and an assorted nigiri set from the chef.
nodes.em3_s1_14: Behind the counter, the chef—a man past fifty—answered with a brisk nod, lifted a translucent fillet of whitefish from a wooden box, rested his left index and middle fingers lightly atop the flesh, and took up a long, gleaming yanagiba knife in his right hand.
nodes.em3_s1_15: The instant the blade met the grain of the fish, his wrist drew back in one level stroke—not a hint of sawing hesitation, the entire length of steel gliding smoothly from heel to tip in a single draw. Paper-thin sashimi settled effortlessly off the flat of the blade, its cut surface gleaming like a mirror under the warm lamp without a single crushed fiber or frayed edge.
nodes.em3_s1_16: Beside him, watching the follow-through of that stroke, Emiko Mido breathed two words almost by pure reflex:
nodes.em3_s1_18: Following her gaze to the cutting board, Ryuji couldn't help a quiet smile—even out of her white coat and outside the hospital walls, the surgical chief was still staring straight at the blade in someone else's hand.
nodes.em3_s1_19: Lowering his voice, Ryuji remarked offhandedly:
nodes.em3_s1_20: "Zero wobble in the bevel angle. He let the rearward draw tension along the full blade part the fibers instead of muscling downward."
nodes.em3_s1_21: Emiko didn't bother denying the occupational habit. Her eyes stayed with the chef's cloth as he wiped the steel, her tone every bit as serious as if she were critiquing an incision in the OR:
nodes.em3_s1_22: "And his wrist didn't flick at the exit. Most people rush to lift the tip on the final millimeter and leave a shallow step along the lower margin—his stroke stayed in a single plane from start to finish."
nodes.em3_s1_23: "Textbook single-pass division. Whatever the trade, whether a pair of hands is steady shows at a glance."
nodes.em3_s1_24: The counter was narrow, and restrained as their low exchange was, every word carried clearly across to the board.
nodes.em3_s1_25: Pausing mid-motion over a ball of vinegared rice, the sushi chef looked up to study these two intently focused patrons and offered a faintly curious smile:
nodes.em3_s1_26: "Listening to the two of you talk bevel angles and cut planes… are you in the counter trade yourselves?"
nodes.em3_s1_27: Emiko met the chef's eyes with utter calm:
nodes.em3_s1_29: Dead silence hung behind the counter for two full seconds.
nodes.em3_s1_30: The chef glanced down at the long yanagiba in his hand, then back up at the poised, cool-eyed young woman across from him, and quietly folded his wiping cloth back beside the board:
nodes.em3_s1_31: "…Then if it's all the same to you, I think I'll still slice tonight's fish myself."
nodes.em3_s1_32: Ryuji couldn't hold back a laugh.
nodes.em3_s1_33: Even the ever-cool Emiko had the faintest stir at the corner of her mouth as she gave the chef an earnest nod:
nodes.em3_s1_34: "By all means, please do. When it comes to finishing a draw cut with a single-bevel long blade, my hands truly can't match yours."
nodes.em3_s1_35: The chef let out a hearty laugh, the air loosening at once, set two freshly formed pieces of whitefish nigiri onto the black-glazed ceramic plates before them, and turned toward the back kitchen to check on the miso pot.
nodes.em3_s1_36: Only the soft simmer of the kettle remained in the small shop.
nodes.em3_s1_37: Picking up a piece of nigiri and taking a bite, Ryuji followed the thread of conversation casually:
nodes.em3_s1_38: "Come to think of it, though—in a larger kitchen, the person with the fastest hands and sharpest knife work at the board doesn't always end up being the head chef running the whole house."
nodes.em3_s1_39: Emiko's fingers paused on her chopsticks for a fraction of a second.
nodes.em3_s1_40: She turned her head toward Ryuji, not a trace of coyness in those clear, cool eyes as she cut straight through the subtext:
nodes.em3_s1_41: "You're talking about Hoshimi Hospital's vacant Director of Surgery post?"
nodes.em3_s1_43: "Half the hospital is guessing which of the candidates will end up taking it."
nodes.em3_s1_44: "There's nothing to guess about. I want that post, and I have every right to contend for it."
nodes.em3_s1_45: She said it squarely and without pretense—neither feigning modesty nor lowering her voice.
nodes.em3_s1_46: "I don't care how kitchens do it. In surgery, a director cannot be someone who merely sits in an office signing rosters. When the most forbidding case in the hospital is on the table—or an intraoperative crisis hits that nobody else can contain—the person wearing the director's title has to be capable of stepping up and taking the scalpel personally."
nodes.em3_s1_48: "I won't argue with that. If the person at the top can't command the hardest table, the surgeons underneath never truly feel steady. Still—"
nodes.em3_s1_49: Meeting her gaze, he stated the other half of the equation just as calmly:
nodes.em3_s1_50: "A department isn't running its single hardest operation every hour of every day. Keeping multiple rooms moving in parallel, pairing surgeons of different seniority, bringing up juniors, coordinating the floor when two emergencies collide at once—if you weigh all of that, Deputy Chief Artoria's command over a team isn't just for show either."
nodes.em3_s1_51: At the name "Artoria," Emiko lifted her hot tea, her gaze sharpening ever so slightly above the rim of the cup.
nodes.em3_s1_52: "Her organizational command is genuinely strong. Nobody in the department calculates more cleanly than she does when it comes to putting each person where mistakes are least likely—I acknowledge that. There's no point pretending not to see it."
nodes.em3_s_01: She conceded the point cleanly—yet in the very next breath her tone pivoted, her eyes coming back to rest on Ryuji's face as though asking purely in passing:
nodes.em3_s_02: "…Though you certainly seem to have a thorough read on how she operates."
nodes.em3_s_05: Lowering her lashes to blow a fleck of foam off her tea, Emiko kept her voice nearly flat, only the faintest edge glinting on the tail of the sentence:
nodes.em3_s_06: "On the schedule board earlier, didn't you already have her stand in your first-assistant spot? Tell me—did the two of you mesh comfortably?"
nodes.em3_s_07: The air stalled for a subtle half-beat.
nodes.em3_s_08: She delivered it so naturally that for a moment Ryuji could hardly tell whether she minded a rival earning high marks from him—or simply cared a little too much about who stood directly across his operating table.
nodes.em3_o_01: She conceded the point cleanly and took a sip from her coarse ceramic cup. Just when the subject seemed settled, her tone pivoted as she set the cup down, her eyes coming back to rest on Ryuji's face:
nodes.em3_o_02: "…Come to think of it, in that recent operation you led, it was {recent_assistant_doctor} standing in your first-assistant spot, wasn't it?"
nodes.em3_o_04: "Hm? What brought that up all of a sudden?"
nodes.em3_o_05: Lowering her lashes to blow a fleck of foam off her tea, Emiko kept her voice perfectly level:
nodes.em3_o_06: "Nothing in particular. Just observing what sort of standard you use when choosing a partner."
nodes.em3_o_07: The air stalled for a subtle half-beat.
nodes.em3_o_08: Every syllable sounded strictly businesslike—only the half-second pause of her fingertips against the wall of the teacup betrayed the faintest trace of an edge.
nodes.em3_g_01: She conceded the point cleanly and took a sip from her coarse ceramic cup. Just when the subject seemed settled, her tone pivoted as she set the cup down, her eyes coming back to rest on Ryuji's face:
nodes.em3_g_02: "…You certainly put plenty of thought into how tables are paired."
nodes.em3_g_05: Lowering her lashes to blow a fleck of foam off her tea, Emiko kept her voice nearly devoid of inflection:
nodes.em3_g_06: "Now that my name is on your regular roster too, I'm rather curious to see whom you'll choose to put in the first-assistant spot from here on."
nodes.em3_g_07: The air stalled for a subtle half-beat.
nodes.em3_g_08: Every syllable sounded strictly businesslike—only the half-second pause of her fingertips along the rim of the teacup betrayed the faintest trace of an edge.
nodes.em3_c1a_02: "Considering a certain surgical chief wouldn't even let me write her name onto a regular schedule until she handed out an eighty-eight the other day, you can hardly blame me for a late start on routine pairings."
nodes.em3_c1a_03: Emiko shot him a cool sidelong glance:
nodes.em3_c1a_04: "That was because I hadn't confirmed you were worth scheduling yet."
nodes.em3_c1a_s_01: "As for style—scrubbing with Artoria really does take weight off your mind, since she keeps every peripheral handoff seamless. Still, when it comes to a razor-thin fight where not a millimeter can slip, I know full well what it means to have you standing across the table."
nodes.em3_c1a_og_01: "Anyone in the department can see how seamlessly Artoria keeps the surrounding pieces in order; when it comes down to a razor-thin fight on the table where not a millimeter can slip, though, I know full well what it means to have you across from me."
nodes.em3_c1a_tail_01: Her fingertips around the teacup eased by an almost imperceptible degree, though her tongue spared him nothing:
nodes.em3_c1a_tail_02: "At least you haven't muddled the arithmetic."
nodes.em3_c1b_01: Ryuji arched a brow, looking over at her with a trace of unhurried amusement:
nodes.em3_c1b_02: "Here I never imagined Chief Mido would go out of her way to notice who stands in my first-assistant spot."
nodes.em3_c1b_03: Emiko met his gaze without so much as a flutter of her eyelashes:
nodes.em3_c1b_04: "I'm the surgical chief. Reviewing the fourth-floor schedule board every day is part of my job."
nodes.em3_c1b_05: She paused half a second and set her teacup lightly back onto its wooden coaster:
nodes.em3_c1b_06: "Besides, having just given you an eighty-eight, I ought to check whether your eye for surgical partners starts slipping afterward."
nodes.em3_c1b_07: An airtight cover—except that she reached for her tea half a beat faster than before.
nodes.em3_c1c_01: Ryuji kept his expression open and matter-of-fact:
nodes.em3_c1c_02: "When you work in the same surgical department, you have to see clearly what each person excels at. Everyone on the floor can see how Artoria binds a ten-person team into a single unit—and as for how fast and how steady your blade is, nobody has seen that more clearly at the table than I have."
nodes.em3_c1c_03: Emiko raised her eyes to him, a whisper of satisfaction passing across their cool depths:
nodes.em3_c1c_04: "Breaking the two of us down side by side? Quite the nerve."
nodes.em3_c1c_05: "Just calling it honestly. Neither of your strengths is exactly a secret."
nodes.em3_c1c_07: "At least your eyes aren't just for decoration."
nodes.em3_s1r_01: The sushi chef returned to set two steaming bowls of red miso soup before them, then withdrew once more to tidy up in the back.
nodes.em3_s1r_02: Taking his bowl, Ryuji brought the subject cleanly to rest:
nodes.em3_s1r_03: "So I'm not casting an early vote for anyone on the directorship. Whether it's your blade that locks down a crisis or her command that steadies the whole floor, the real proof will settle it in the end."
nodes.em3_s1r_04: Studying his calm, candid profile, Emiko fell silent for two seconds before speaking with crisp clarity:
nodes.em3_s1r_05: "You don't need to cast a vote for anyone."
nodes.em3_s1r_06: "If you earn the standing to put your own name on that shortlist someday, then we compete fairly. I won't yield an inch to you."
nodes.em3_s1r_07: Ryuji met her gaze and nodded:
nodes.em3_s1r_09: Finishing the last piece of nigiri on her plate, Emiko wiped her fingertips clean with a warm towel and turned toward the man beside her—almost as if only now recalling a routine piece of business:
nodes.em3_s1r_10: "Tomorrow morning at nine in Operating Room One, there's a coronary artery bypass graft. Multivessel disease—median sternotomy, on-pump CABG."
nodes.em3_s1r_13: "Yes. I've already held the first-assistant slot on the board for you."
nodes.em3_s1r_14: This time, she didn't call it a "test," nor did she ask whether he had the nerve to take it.
nodes.em3_s1r_15: Rising from her stool and picking up her trench coat, Emiko looked down at Ryuji beside the counter, her voice brief and certain:
nodes.em3_s1r_16: "Get to sleep early tonight, and bring both your eyes and your hands sharp to the table tomorrow."
nodes.em3_s1r_17: "How a true major thoracic case is opened at Hoshimi Hospital—tomorrow, I'll show you myself."
nodes.em3_s2_01: Early the next morning, Operating Room One carried a dense, exacting weight markedly heavier than that of a routine abdominal case.
nodes.em3_s2_02: Along the right wall, the roller pumps and oxygenator circuit of the heart-lung machine were already primed, the perfusionist running a final microbubble check and heater-cooler calibration; at the head of the table, green ECG waveforms and red invasive arterial pressure traces marched across the anesthesia monitor in brisker electronic ticks than usual.
nodes.em3_s2_03: The twenty-seven-year-old female patient lay at the center of the operating table. She had signed a thick stack of consent forms during her preoperative consultation, yet actually lying inside the main suite surrounded by bypass hardware and sternal instruments—listening to staff confirm blood units and cardioplegia parameters in low voices—had drained every trace of color from her face.
nodes.em3_s2_04: Moe Honjo had barely tucked the warming blanket around her shoulders when the patient's fingers clamped white-knuckled onto the edge of the sheet beneath her, sending the heart-rate readout jumping more than a dozen beats.
nodes.em3_s2_05: Moe spoke gently to soothe her:
nodes.em3_s2_06: "Take a slow breath, try not to tense up—the anesthesiologist will help you drift right off to sleep in just a moment…"
nodes.em3_s2_07: As if unable to process the words, the woman stared past the rail toward Emiko Mido checking coronary angiogram films beside the console, her lips trembling violently as her eyes welled red:
nodes.em3_s2_08: "Dr. Mido… I heard them checking the machine over there… Are you really about to saw my breastbone open and make my heart stop beating…?"
nodes.em3_s2_09: Her voice shook almost out of pitch, raw with the unfiltered terror of an adult confronting life and death:
nodes.em3_s2_10: "What if… what if once it stops, it never starts beating again…? I could die on this table…"
nodes.em3_s2_11: Every quiet murmur across the operating room stilled at once.
nodes.em3_s2_12: Setting down the coronary angiography folder, Emiko didn't offer platitudes from across the floor. She walked straight to the right side of the table and leaned in so that those clear, unclouded eyes filled the patient's line of sight.
nodes.em3_s2_13: She didn't raise her voice, yet through the surgical mask every syllable landed like forged steel, severing the rising panic cleanly:
nodes.em3_s2_15: Holding her breath, the patient stared back at her.
nodes.em3_s2_16: "Today, I lead the table. You will not die."
nodes.em3_s2_17: No cheap "it's only a minor procedure," and no dodging the gravity of open-chest bypass itself—only the absolute composure of a surgeon who had already shouldered the full weight of the operation.
nodes.em3_s2_18: On the monitor, the racing heart rate visibly eased down in the wake of that single declaration.
nodes.em3_s2_19: Rather than stepping back right away, Emiko angled half a step aside, drawing attention naturally toward Ryuji Sakaguchi beside her as she spoke openly before the patient and the entire team:
nodes.em3_s2_20: "Standing across from me is Dr. Sakaguchi—the first assistant I personally chose for your operation today."
nodes.em3_s2_21: "His hands are more than worthy of this spot. Anesthesia, perfusion, and nursing are all in position—all you need to do is close your eyes and sleep. Leave the rest to us."
nodes.em3_s2_22: Beside her, Ryuji met the patient's eyes with a steady, reassuring nod:
nodes.em3_s2_23: "Rest easy. By the time you wake up, the new bridges will already be carrying blood."
nodes.em3_s2_24: Looking up at the two rock-steady surgeons beside her bed, the woman slowly unclenched her white-knuckled grip on the sheet and gave a thick, tearful nod:
nodes.em3_s2_25: "…Okay. I'm counting on you, Dr. Mido… and on you too, Dr. Sakaguchi."
nodes.em3_s2_26: Straightening up, Emiko issued a crisp command to the room:
nodes.em3_s2_28: "Patient identity confirmed—twenty-seven-year-old female, severe multivessel coronary stenosis scheduled for elective median-sternotomy on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting. Crossmatched and autologous blood units verified!"
nodes.em3_s2_29: "Cardiopulmonary bypass circuit prime, oxygenator, heater-cooler unit, and cardioplegia delivery pump self-checks normal—ready to go on bypass at your call."
nodes.em3_s2_30: "Sternal entry set, internal mammary retractor, micro-coronary instruments, fine vascular sutures, and internal defibrillator paddles counted and ready."
nodes.em3_s2_31: "Invasive arterial line and central venous access patent. Starting intravenous general anesthesia induction now."
nodes.em3_s2_32: A clear mask settled gently over the patient's nose and mouth; as milky induction agent flowed into the line, her eyelids drifted shut and her breathing soon deepened into an even rhythm.
nodes.em3_s2_33: Once anesthetic depth was confirmed and the endotracheal tube was secured to the ventilator, Emiko and Ryuji stepped out to the scrub sinks for a full surgical scrub—returning through the foot-pedal doors to don crisp sterile gowns and double sterile gloves with Hiroko Sugimura and Moe Honjo assisting.
nodes.em3_s3_01: The overhead surgical lights converged along the midline sternal mark.
nodes.em3_s3_02: Emiko incised the presternal skin and subcutaneous fascia, then guided the sternal saw steadily down the midline to divide the sternum longitudinally; Hiroko passed bone wax and electrocautery forceps without a wasted motion while Ryuji achieved meticulous hemostasis along the marrow and periosteal edges opposite her, before the sternal retractor opened a clear anterior mediastinal field.
nodes.em3_s3_03: Next came the foundational test of patience prior to cardiopulmonary bypass—harvesting the pedicled left internal mammary artery (LIMA) and verifying caliber match against the prepared saphenous vein conduit.
nodes.em3_s3_04: Through the opening quarter hour, Emiko kept to her usual spare, incisive teaching cadence:
nodes.em3_s3_05: "Raise the IMA retractor another half-notch. This artery is the cornerstone conduit for long-term patency—leave an adequate fascial pedicle off the main trunk, clip the side branches with small titanium clips, keep cautery low, and never risk thermal injury to the intima."
nodes.em3_s3_06: "Understood. Proximal first intercostal branch is exposed—small clip applier ready."
nodes.em3_s3_08: Once the full length of the pedicled LIMA was mobilized and directional markings on the flushed vein graft were confirmed, the two incised and suspended the pericardium into a level pericardial cradle, bringing the beating heart and ascending aorta cleanly into the center of the field.
nodes.em3_s3_09: Checking the epicardial course of the coronaries, Emiko ran one final pre-bypass target confirmation with Ryuji across the table:
nodes.em3_s3_10: "Matches the angiogram. Distal mid-LAD takes the LIMA as our primary target, and the posterolateral obtuse marginal takes the vein graft—distal vein anastomosis on the lateral wall first, then LIMA-to-LAD, and the proximal aortic anastomosis last. Clear on the sequence?"
nodes.em3_s3_11: Ryuji scanned the epicardial target zones:
nodes.em3_s3_12: "Exposing the obtuse marginal after arrest requires lifting and rotating the apex—completing that graft first means we never tug on the anterior LIMA anastomosis afterward. Completely sound."
nodes.em3_s3_13: Above her mask, Emiko's brow shifted a fraction, sparing any extra commentary:
nodes.em3_s3_15: "Systemic heparin bolus complete—repeat ACT has reached safe cardiopulmonary bypass threshold."
nodes.em3_s3_16: With heparinization confirmed, Emiko cleanly divided the distal LIMA, briefly released control to verify brisk pulsatile free flow before securing it with an atraumatic bull-dog clamp, then placed double purse-string sutures on the distal ascending aorta and right atrium with swift, rock-steady hands; Ryuji controlled the tourniquet snuggers opposite her as she seated the aortic arterial cannula and cavoatrial venous cannula, de-aired meticulously, and locked the lines onto the bypass circuit.
nodes.em3_s3_18: "Copy, initiating cardiopulmonary bypass—venous return smooth, ramping pump flow to full calculated index, mean perfusion pressure stable!"
nodes.em3_s3_19: As dark venous blood drained into the oxygenator and returned bright arterial crimson into the ascending aorta, the workload eased off the chambers and the operation crossed into its most unforgiving, time-critical core.
nodes.em3_s3_20: "Prepare to cross-clamp the ascending aorta. Cardioplegia line ready."
nodes.em3_s3_22: An atraumatic aortic cross-clamp closed squarely across the distal ascending aorta as high-potassium cold blood cardioplegia coursed through the root needle into the coronary bed, while iced saline slush pads were nestled into the pericardial well to protect the myocardium.
nodes.em3_s3_23: Within seconds, the ECG trace flattened into a quiet line. The heart that had been beating powerfully inside the chest relaxed into complete stillness, leaving only the low, rhythmic hum of the bypass roller pumps in the room.
nodes.em3_s3_24: "Cross-clamp timer running—initial cardioplegia dose delivered, complete electromechanical arrest achieved."
nodes.em3_s3_25: From the second the cross-clamp clicked shut, every passing minute was myocardial ischemic time—permitting neither frantic haste nor ten seconds lost to wasted motion.
nodes.em3_s3_26: Cradling the arrested heart gently through a warm moist pad with his left hand, Ryuji rotated the deep posterolateral left ventricular target smoothly into the exact focal point of the overhead lamps.
nodes.em3_s3_27: Hiroko passed the pointed scalpel and Potts coronary scissors:
nodes.em3_s3_29: Leaning in through her surgical loupes over an anterior vessel wall barely two millimeters across, Emiko held her wrists steady as precision-machined steel—nicking the wall cleanly with the tip of the blade and extending a crisp, millimeter-true longitudinal arteriotomy with the Potts scissors without a tremor.
nodes.em3_s3_30: And in the single-second interval as she finished the cut and reached to exchange for her Castroviejo micro-needle holder, something quietly shifted.
nodes.em3_s3_31: "Trim the distal vein graft to a—"
nodes.em3_s3_32: Before she was halfway through the phrase, Ryuji had already presented the forty-five-degree beveled heel of the vein graft squarely along the axis of the arteriotomy five millimeters ahead of her needle tip with fine forceps, while the misted CO2 blower-suction in his other hand cleared a single residual droplet of cardioplegia to leave the gossamer coronary intima razor-sharp in view.
nodes.em3_s3_33: The rest of Emiko's sentence stopped at her lips.
nodes.em3_s3_34: Lifting her gaze half an inch through her loupes for one brief look at the man across from her, she added not a word and drove home the first hair-fine 7-0 polypropylene stitch.
nodes.em3_s3_35: One throw, two throws—a continuous parachute run.
nodes.em3_s3_36: There was no longer any need to call out "follow," "give me half a centimeter," or "clear the edge." The instant Emiko's wrist rolled the needle out, Ryuji's shod forceps caught the loop with supple, unvarying tension that never cut the vessel wall; the split second before she pivoted into the tightest heel angle, his fingers cradling the myocardium had already adjusted the tilt by two degrees, laying the posterior lip flat before her loupes.
nodes.em3_s3_37: When they moved to the second target—the critical LIMA-to-LAD anastomosis—the chosen LAD segment lay nested inside a shallow groove bordered by thick epicardial fat whose margins kept creeping inward over the suture line.
nodes.em3_c2a_01: Without waiting for Emiko to spare attention on the encroaching fat, Ryuji kept the heart steady with his left hand while taking a warm-saline micro-pledget and atraumatic forceps from Hiroko's tray with his right—gently parting and padding both thick epicardial borders back so the entire posterior wall of the LAD lumen lay flat in the dead center of her loupes.
nodes.em3_c2a_02: Emiko's Castroviejo needle holder didn't hesitate for half a beat, gliding straight down the lane he had opened through the heel of the LIMA-to-LAD anastomosis.
nodes.em3_c2a_03: Between throws, head bowed over the field, she murmured two quiet words almost without realizing it:
nodes.em3_c2a_05: Devoid of grading stiffness or scrutiny—so soft it sounded like pure, unguarded appreciation at how effortlessly two pairs of hands were meshing.
nodes.em3_c2b_01: Guarding the epicardial margin along the LAD arteriotomy with micro-forceps, Ryuji offered the key spatial cue in half a breath:
nodes.em3_c2b_02: "LIMA pedicle lies flat with zero twist and half a centimeter of diastolic slack—entering the heel straight from eleven o'clock gives the cleanest run."
nodes.em3_c2b_03: Scanning the pedicle arc and arteriotomy alignment through her loupes in a single glance and confirming it matched her own judgment to the millimeter, Emiko dispensed with any redundant verbal cue and drove the needle cleanly in at eleven o'clock:
nodes.em3_c2b_04: "Exactly what I had in mind. Hold this left strand."
nodes.em3_c2b_06: Fine monofilament drew snugly down under the lamps, everting both arterial intimal edges into seamless apposition. Studying an anastomotic ring nearly sculptural in its smoothness, Emiko spoke under her breath:
nodes.em3_c2b_07: "…Very good. Scrubbing with you really does save breath."
nodes.em3_c2c_01: Holding crisp micro-tension across the LAD margins while eyeing the burr-free bevel Emiko had fashioned on the LIMA in a single snip of the Potts scissors, Ryuji followed her suture without missing a beat and murmured:
nodes.em3_c2c_02: "Single plane edge to edge, not a millimeter of step—even last night's sushi chef would tip his hat to that cut."
nodes.em3_c2c_03: Behind the instrument table, catching that cryptic bit of shop talk, Hiroko's eyes curved faintly above her mask.
nodes.em3_c2c_04: As Emiko's needle holder passed the final anterior stitch through the LAD wall, the rarest whisper of amusement touched the cool corner of her eye:
nodes.em3_c2c_05: "Don't compare sashimi to an internal mammary artery… though your accuracy following suture hasn't slowed my blade down, I'll grant you that. …Good. Prepare to de-air and tie."
nodes.em3_s3r_01: As the final loop of 8-0 suture settled gently home, the core LIMA-to-LAD anastomosis was complete.
nodes.em3_s3r_02: Immediately afterward, maintaining the bloodless field under aortic cross-clamp, Ryuji exposed a plaque-free anterior segment of the ascending aorta and assisted Emiko in punching a clean aortotomy window, completing a tight proximal vein-graft anastomosis and de-airing micro-bubbles from the conduit.
nodes.em3_s3r_03: "Cross-clamp duration right on target, systemic rewarming complete—ready to release the aortic cross-clamp."
nodes.em3_s3r_04: "Vent and suction ready, watch ventricular filling and graft perfusion closely—release the cross-clamp."
nodes.em3_s3r_05: The ascending aortic cross-clamp eased open.
nodes.em3_s3r_06: Warm, crimson arterial blood surged instantly into the native coronaries and both newly constructed bypass conduits! Pale, silent myocardium flushed deep living rose before their eyes—and within barely a dozen seconds, without even needing internal defibrillator paddles, the ventricular fibers gave a light tremor followed by two strong thumps, snapping straight back into vigorous spontaneous contractions!
nodes.em3_s3r_07: "ECG back in regular sinus rhythm! ST segments settling cleanly, airway compliance good—resuming bilateral lung ventilation!"
nodes.em3_s3r_08: The taut atmospheric pressure that had gripped the room all morning eased at once, Moe letting out a quiet breath beside the charting desk.
nodes.em3_s3r_09: "Ventricular contractility and filling look great—stepping cardiopulmonary bypass flow down in stages now: half flow… quarter flow… off pump! Clean separation from bypass!"
nodes.em3_s3r_10: Native circulation assumed full systemic perfusion.
nodes.em3_s3r_11: Neither surgeon rushed to decannulate; with the chambers full and beating under physiologic pressure, they inspected both conduits methodically from proximal hood to distal toe—both the LIMA and saphenous vein lay plump and smoothly contoured without kink, bounding pulsatile flow unmistakable beneath a light fingertip, every needle hole dry and both the posterior pericardium and retrosternal bed free of active oozing.
nodes.em3_s3r_12: Confirming zero need for revision, Emiko and Ryuji removed the venous and arterial cannulae in sequence and reinforced the purse-strings as anesthesia administered protamine to reverse heparin; once pericardial and mediastinal chest tubes were seated, Hiroko and Moe completed the pre-closure count.
nodes.em3_s3r_13: "Pre-closure count—lap pads, micro-pledgets, bull-dog clamps, needles, and all instruments verified correct by dual check!"
nodes.em3_s3r_14: "Circulating count sheet matches across the board!"
nodes.em3_s3r_15: Stainless-steel sternal wires drew the two halves of the sternum snugly back into apposition, followed by layered closure of fascia and subcutis; as Hiroko and Moe called out a clean final closing count, the skin incision was neatly completed.
nodes.em3_s3r_16: By the time sterile dressing settled along the midline sternotomy and invasive arterial pressure held rock-steady in the target range, the demanding open-chest bypass had reached an exemplary finish.
nodes.em3_s4_01: Having verified the transport ventilator, portable monitor, and chest-drain suction, the anesthesiologist and Moe wheeled the hemodynamically stable patient smoothly toward the ICU for handover; Hiroko packed the micro-cardiac instrument trays, offered both surgeons a warm "great work today," and rolled the case cart out of Operating Room One.
nodes.em3_s4_02: With hours of razor-edged concentration finally lifted, Ryuji rolled his stiff shoulders, stepped over to review the perfusion timestamps, and turned casually toward Emiko beside him:
nodes.em3_s4_03: "Right before we came off bypass, when the right ventricle filled back out, the arc on that posterolateral vein graft settled in without a millimeter too much or too little slack—I wanted to ask a quick question about how you gauged that length—"
nodes.em3_s4_04: Halfway through the sentence, Ryuji stopped.
nodes.em3_s4_05: Standing in the dimmed glow of the surgical lamps, Emiko Mido showed not the slightest trace of fatigue from hours at an open-chest cardiac table.
nodes.em3_s4_06: Quite the opposite: even though the operation was completely over and the patient safely out the door, she stood like a bowstring drawn to its absolute limit on stage—not slackening with chest closure at all, but radiating a quiet, almost searing tautness.
nodes.em3_s4_07: She didn't glance at the record sheet in Ryuji's hand. Her eyes lingered on the empty operating table as her fingertip gave one faint tap against the rim of the metal instrument mayo stand, before she turned and issued a dismissal:
nodes.em3_s4_10: "Not finishing the operative log right now while we're here?"
nodes.em3_s4_11: "Wait for me in the doctors' office. I'm staying in the operating room alone for a little while—head out first."
nodes.em3_s4_12: Her tone remained as cool and clipped as ever, offering zero explanation and leaving zero room for discussion.
nodes.em3_s4_13: Less than twenty minutes ago in this very room, she had allowed another surgeon to share the exact rhythm of her breathing across millimeter-scale coronary sutures for the first time; yet the instant the curtain fell, she retreated behind that invisible boundary line and shut him squarely outside.
nodes.em3_s4_14: Ryuji looked at her for two quiet seconds, asked nothing further, and nodded:
nodes.em3_s4_15: "Got it. I'll go change first—see you in the office later."
nodes.em3_s4_16: Emiko gave the faintest murmur in reply:
nodes.em3_s4_18: Ryuji stepped out of Operating Room One.
nodes.em3_s4_19: Behind him came the low hush of the automatic track—the heavy operating room doors sealing tight without a seam, shutting the surgical chief alone inside along with that corner of herself no one was permitted to enter behind the frosted glass.
nodes.em3_s5_01: After grabbing a quick shower, changing back into his white coat, and swinging by the ICU to confirm the patient's steady chest-tube output and hemodynamics, Ryuji returned to the surgical doctors' workroom with his drafted operative notes tucked under his arm.
nodes.em3_s5_02: The surgical chief's desk by the window stood empty. When he walked down the hall to pour a cup of hot coffee in the staff lounge, Emiko Mido wasn't there either.
nodes.em3_s5_03: Rather than doubling back to the fourth-floor surgical suite to pry, Ryuji returned to his desk, opened his notebook, and jotted down the key tension nuances from today's LAD and saphenous vein anastomoses point by point.
nodes.em3_s5_04: He glanced up at the wall clock—nearly thirty minutes had passed since they parted outside Operating Room One before the office door finally pushed lightly open.
nodes.em3_s5_06: She had changed back into her immaculate, crisp white coat, her long hair smoothed into flawless order once more and her stride as composed as ever. Only as she pulled out her desk chair did her motion seem half a beat slower than usual, the fingers of her right hand unconsciously smoothing a lapel edge that was already buttoned to perfection before she sat.
nodes.em3_s5_07: Looking up, Ryuji greeted her casually:
nodes.em3_s5_08: "Back? Didn't see you in the lounge when I grabbed coffee earlier—figured you'd gone straight to check the ward."
nodes.em3_s5_09: Eyes lowered as she opened her drawer for a fountain pen, Emiko sidestepped the implied question in two words:
nodes.em3_s5_12: "More or less. After a major table, I'm used to sitting somewhere quiet by myself for a bit."
nodes.em3_s5_13: She offered not a syllable of detail, her voice as matter-of-fact as a remark on the weather—except that as she opened a folder on her desk, her fingertip lingered a split second on the blank margin, as though her thoughts hadn't quite finished detaching from the undertow of that solitude.
nodes.em3_s5_14: Taking it in without pressing a single question about what could possibly keep someone behind closed OR doors for half an hour, Ryuji picked up his notebook naturally, walked over, and spread his sketch on the corner of her desk:
nodes.em3_s5_15: "Perfect timing, then, while today's feel is still fresh in my hands—let me ask that practical question. During our filling check right before coming off bypass, the moment the right ventricle expanded, that posterolateral vein graft lay smoothly along the epicardium without the slightest kink. When you measured length earlier, how did you calculate that chamber-expansion shift so precisely?"
nodes.em3_s5_16: The instant the question landed, every trace of lingering abstraction vanished from Emiko Mido.
nodes.em3_s5_17: Her eyes locked straight onto his sketch from ascending aorta to obtuse marginal; taking a pencil, she drew two decisive arcs across the aortic root and right ventricular outflow tract, her voice snapping back to its usual blade-sharp precision:
nodes.em3_s5_18: "A decompressed, arrested heart and a heart carrying physiologic pressure on its own are two completely different three-dimensional geometries."
nodes.em3_s5_19: "Plenty of novices measure a vein graft on an empty, flaccid heart so it looks straight and tidy, only to watch the right ventricle and pulmonary trunk balloon up on weaning from bypass and buckle the conduit into an acute kink—while leaving too much slack makes it fold under the pericardium once you wire the sternum shut."
nodes.em3_s5_20: The tip of her pencil tapped squarely on the inflection point of the diagram:
nodes.em3_s5_21: "So you never wait until weaning off pump to trust luck. Before cutting proximal length and punching the aortic window, you factor in the full expansion arc of the refilled right ventricle up front and angle the proximal hood roughly thirty degrees off the flow tangent—then run one final lie check as pump flow comes down and the chambers refill. Miss either step, and the cleanest distal suturing in the world goes to waste."
nodes.em3_s5_22: Airtight logic and unforgiving standards—every word forged out of hundreds of hours at the table.
nodes.em3_s5_23: Nodding inwardly as he took it in, Ryuji gathered his sketch with a genuine note of admiration:
nodes.em3_s5_24: "Factoring even post-closure pericardial compression into the aortotomy angle beforehand… no wonder standing through an operation that size doesn't seem to tire you in the slightest."
nodes.em3_s5_25: Emiko's fingers stilled briefly on her fountain pen as she lifted a cool glance toward him:
nodes.em3_s5_26: "Didn't I tell you once already? I simply happen to like surgery."
nodes.em3_s5_27: Word for word the same understatement she had used after their very first operation together—yet here it resonated like a layered echo, unimpeachably candid while keeping the private door behind it sealed tight.
nodes.em3_s6_01: Jotting down her notes on right-ventricular expansion allowance and proximal hood angulation, Ryuji capped his pen, met Emiko's cool gaze, and—recalling how their previous two operations had ended—asked half in jest:
nodes.em3_s6_02: "That covers the technical questions. So, Chief Mido—what score does your first assistant get today? Eighty-five the first time I assisted you, eighty-eight last time when I took primary—surely I've grazed ninety today?"
nodes.em3_s6_03: Emiko's hand paused, and she looked up at him quietly.
nodes.em3_s6_04: Afternoon sunlight slanting through the office window rested across her pale, composed profile. This time, she neither rattled off an exacting number nor picked apart his first five minutes at the table.
nodes.em3_s6_05: After a brief two-second silence, she spoke evenly:
nodes.em3_s6_10: Reaching to the edge of her desk, she drew out a hardcover binder marked with a blue ribbon—her own handwritten manual on CABG conduit planning and cardiopulmonary bypass transition checkpoints, crisp fountain-pen annotations lining its margins—and slid it casually across to the edge of the desk before Ryuji.
nodes.em3_s6_11: "You aren't here taking an exam anymore."
nodes.em3_s6_12: Ryuji glanced down at the private operative notebook she would never ordinarily lend a soul, then looked back up at the woman across from him.
nodes.em3_s6_13: Her expression remained poised and unsentimental, devoid of forced softness, adding a practical postscript in the tone one surgeon uses with an equal:
nodes.em3_s6_14: "Look through the notes inside on cardioplegia timing and proximal hood angles first—if there are verification steps you want to add, write them straight in the margins. Next time a coronary bypass case comes up on the regular schedule, whether you're primary or I am, we prep to this standard."
nodes.em3_s6_15: Pausing briefly, she even asked his opinion on her own initiative:
nodes.em3_s6_16: "Out of curiosity—today's sequence of sewing the posterolateral vein graft first and the LIMA-to-LAD second: if you had been standing in the primary spot, would you have changed it?"
nodes.em3_s6_17: Ryuji considered it seriously for a moment:
nodes.em3_s6_18: "Given how much apical displacement today's patient needed, I wouldn't change a thing. Finishing the posterior target that demands heavy cardiac rotation before touching the delicate LIMA carries the lowest risk."
nodes.em3_s6_19: Emiko gave an almost imperceptible nod:
nodes.em3_s6_20: "It seems our judgment matches on that count."
nodes.em3_s6_21: Ryuji picked up the weighty blue binder. Looking across at the surgical chief as she reached for her next chart, he knew unmistakably that from this moment forward he was no longer an examinee being weighed and scored in her eyes, but someone standing squarely on the same side of the table beside her.
nodes.em3_s6_22: Just before he turned back toward his own desk, however, Emiko called his name again.
nodes.em3_s6_26: Emiko raised her eyes, clear and keen, circling lightly back to the subject from last night's sushi counter:
nodes.em3_s6_27: "Sharing technique with you is one thing. As for the Director of Surgery post, my stance hasn't changed."
nodes.em3_s6_28: Not a trace of softening from an exhilarating morning of seamless teamwork, nor half a hint of stepping aside for anyone.
nodes.em3_c3a_01: Expression steady, Ryuji met her gaze squarely:
nodes.em3_c3a_02: "Then we settle it on merit. When the day comes that my name goes on that shortlist, I won't hold back either."
nodes.em3_c3a_03: Unconcealed appreciation flashed across Emiko's eyes:
nodes.em3_c3b_02: "Don't worry—I never planned on anyone yielding to me. Until a winner's decided, though, when another fight like today's lands in the OR, remember to call me."
nodes.em3_c3b_03: Emiko held his gaze for a beat, her answer as crisp as ever:
nodes.em3_c3b_04: "Provided you can keep pace when the time comes."
nodes.em3_c3c_01: Ryuji lifted the blue binder lightly in his hand:
nodes.em3_c3c_02: "Having just lent me your prized bypass notes, Chief Mido, aren't you afraid I'll master them and turn around to challenge you with them someday?"
nodes.em3_c3c_03: Emiko's brow arched slightly, pride ringing clear in her reply:
nodes.em3_c3c_04: "If learning from a single case were enough to beat me, that directorship wouldn't belong to me in the first place. Feel free to try."
nodes.em3_s6r_01: Lowering her gaze to uncap her fountain pen, Emiko glanced over the primary-surgeon and first-assistant signature lines on the newly filed CABG operative record, the faintest, almost imperceptible—yet unmistakably genuine—smile curving the corner of her lips:
nodes.em3_s6r_02: "Of course. Don't expect me to yield to you."
nodes.em3_s6r_03: Smiling lightly, Ryuji tucked the blue binder lined with her handwritten notes under his arm and walked back to his own desk.
nodes.em3_s6r_04: Afternoon sunlight lay quiet across the short stretch of floor between their two desks.
nodes.em3_s6r_05: Head bowed over the next chart without looking up again, Emiko Mido still intended to win, still held unshakable confidence in her claim to the highest seat in surgery, and still kept that unspoken secret behind the operating room doors locked squarely in her own hands—
nodes.em3_s6r_06: Only, perhaps even she hadn't quite sorted out for herself yet:
nodes.em3_s6r_07: Since when had the prospect of continuing to step up to even harder operating tables alongside the man across from her become every bit as compelling as proving she was stronger than him?
